newsitem.title: JAPAN: More Japan firms somewhat cautious on economy - EPA.
newsitem.headline: More Japan firms somewhat cautious on economy - EPA.

text.p: Japanese firms believe the economy is recovering, but compared to last quarter, more companies are somewhat cautious about the recovery, the Economic Planning Agency's quarterly corporate survey showed.
The EPA said its business survey index, released on Friday, showed a 12 for the January-March quarter and a two for the April-June quarter after standing at eight for the October-December quarter.
The index is calculated by subtracting the percentage of businesses which see the economy weakening from the percentage which see it strengthening.
The sales tax will be raised to five percent from three percent in April and is widely expected to prompt a slowdown in the economy in the April-June quarter.
But the report also said that corporate profits are expected to continue to improve.
The corporate profit index showed a seven for the January-March quarter and a five for the April-June quarter after five for the October-December quarter.
The EPA surveyed 4,545 firms with capital of over 100 million yen in December, of which 95.5 percent replied.
